environment.description: Chromium from Playwright on the production build under /getmath/, cold cache (a new browser context for every run), viewport 1280 by 800. Network: 150 ms round trip, 1600 kbit/s down, 750 kbit/s up (the slow 4G profile of Lighthouse), set through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Processor: 4 times slower. Each run loads the page, then waits until no request is in flight and none has started for 500 ms (a failed or pending request fails the run). It submits a prediction, so that the sum, its copy, the formula and the feedback are all shown. It presses 20 arrow keys on a handle, then drags the handle through 30 pointer moves from the middle of one grid cell to the middle of another. Every step must change the arrow, or the run fails. Arrow response is the time from the input to the first frame and the task after it, for every step; the worst of the keyboard also counts the Event Timing figure (it only reports events over 16 ms, in steps of 8 ms), which does not cover pointer moves. The page weight counts bytes as the preview server sends them, without compression, so GitHub Pages sends less.

lcp.label: Largest contentful paint
lcp.why: About 2 times the runner's median of 436 ms and below the public 'good' guidance of 2500 ms. The developer machine's slowest run was 740 ms.

cls.label: Cumulative layout shift
cls.why: The page does not shift at all (0 in every run, in both places). 0.02 is well below the public 'good' guidance of 0.1 and still lets a real shift of the page fail.

keyWorst.label: Keyboard step, worst
keyWorst.why: Provisional until the runner measures the harder run. On the developer machine the median of the runs is 62 ms and the slowest run 106 ms, so the earlier 100 ms was too tight; 150 ms is below the public INP 'good' guidance of 200 ms. The gate compares the median of 3 runs, so one slow step in one run does not fail a pull request.
